kills.flaw: The gap is already crowded by bigger players. Ultra Pro, Vault X and Chinese private labels at $7.99 set the price, landed cost carries about 34% China tariff, and the first sale lands around day 45-60, which misses Q4. AI gives no information or labor edge here that rivals lack. It is plain FBA in a commodity category, which breaks my own kill rule.

Meta keeps the margin, not us. The $55 gross margin runs into a $30-38 median Meta cost per purchase. PSA 8 base-set commons have fully transparent comps, so any gift seller can copy the offer in a week. That leaves $17-25 net per order, so reaching the goal needs about 250 orders a month outside Q4, which the proposal itself calls unlikely.

upgrades.upgrade: Change the weakest route, 'refer for 10% of the shop's buy' (about $120 per close), into selling overflow leads to one vetted dealer per territory at $100-150 per photo-qualified seller, or 5-7% of a closed deal (first-principles-3 pricing). The math behind it: a qualified seller is worth about $900 gross to the dealer at a 40% close rate, about $360 expected. Add marketing-1's comp-receipts report as the closer, and leverage-1's rule to consign lots worth $3k+ at 75/25 instead of buying them (no capital needed). Model exits at 8-10% blended fees. Fanatics weekly auctions charge 0-12%, not 0.

Treat the table waitlist as the mispriced asset. The LA show has about 4,200 vendors waitlisted and Pasadena 375, so raise table prices or sell premium corner and early-setup tables each show until the waitlist shrinks. Run your own 'free AI appraisal, we buy collections' booth at the door so every show doubles as a sourcing channel for business-2 and an exit for its mid-tier lots. Sell sponsor tables to graders, Whatnot sellers and local shops.

Merge it with business-3 into one 'Card Seller Ads Desk'. Lead with the eBay Promoted Listings fee-leak audit, because savings are measurable and easier to sell than growth, then upsell Whatnot Boost and off-platform traffic. Price at 25% of verified savings plus a $500 floor to solve the willingness-to-pay risk. Use the client list as wholesale buyers for business-2's bulk and mid-tier lots.

Don't pay 55-65% across the board, because that gives away the spread, and the spread is the arbitrage. The edge is speed and trust, not price. Offer cash at about 50% and an 80/20 consignment option side by side (business-mind-1). Pay more only on clean slabs, where cert lookup removes most of the risk.

500-2,000 templated set pages risk Google's scaled-content-abuse policy and could get the domain demoted. Build 50-100 deep pages with real checklists and your own sold-price log, and put the effort into the estate-liquidator loop, which is the durable channel.

Price packets from what they are worth to the dealer (about $360 expected value per qualified seller), not cost-plus, and bill the $10k+ tier as a 5-7% finder's fee on close. Put seller consent and an offer-floor policy into the form. Run this as an overflow layer of business-2, not on its own.

$75 per qualified seller against about $60-65 media cost leaves too thin a margin. Price it at $125+ or as a retainer, and bundle it as an overflow route from your own buying desk, so each lead is worth more to you than to any one shop.

Run it only as the Q4 outlet for the collection desk's bulk, not as a standalone business. Ship eBay and TikTok Shop SKUs by Oct 15 to catch the Oct 30 and Nov 6 waves, skip Amazon (gated), and stop after Dec 20.

Use it as the zero-capital cash bridge for the first 60 days. Use AdWhispr to find which US hobby brands are actually advertising (Amazon, Shopify and Meta), and pitch only those, which works around the small reachable pool.

Correction to my own number: Fanatics Collect weekly auctions charge 0-12% depending on format, not '100% of hammer plus bonus', so model exit fees at 8-10% blended. The estate-partner channel and the $750 qualified-value kill switch still hold.

combo: Collection Desk Plus. Core engine is business-2: Google seller-intent ads at $1-5 CPC, Claude photo triage within an hour, and every lead routed by value. Buy at 50% or less of liquid value. Consign $3k+ lots at 75/25 with no capital (leverage-1). Sell overflow and out-of-radius leads to territory dealers at $100-150 each or 5-7% on close (first-principles-3). Decline junk politely with a free report. Closer: marketing-1's comp-receipts estimate. Free supply: 5-10% finder's fees to estate liquidators (growth-1, arbitrage-2). Exits are routed by net fee, with bulk going into demand-2 Q4 gift bundles. Sequence: days 1-60, run arbitrage-1 and mindset-1 for zero-capital cash while a $1.5k ad test proves cost per qualified lead under $150. From month 3, launch a vendor-prepaid local show (business-1) as an owned sourcing and exit channel. Capital is capped at $10-15k, and the kill rule is cost per qualified lead above $300 after 40 leads.
message: The biggest mispricing on the board is attention. Seller-intent clicks cost $1-5 in low competition, while a photo-qualified collection is worth $500-900 gross to whoever buys it. So the winner is the variant that turns every lead into money (buy, consign or sell the lead), not the one that only buys. One correction to my own Round 1: Fanatics weekly auctions charge 0-12%, not 0, so trim the exit margins about 8 points. This gap closes once dealers learn PPC, so spend the next 12 months building owned assets: reviews, a liquidator network and a show brand.
